newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-REID, CLAAR LEAD HAWAIIAN OPEN AFTER FIRST ROUND.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-REID, CLAAR LEAD HAWAIIAN OPEN AFTER FIRST ROUND.

text.p: Mike Reid and Brian Claar shot the lowest rounds of their careers, scores of 10 under par 62 at Waialae C.C., to share the first-round lead of the Hawaiian Open Thursday.
One stroke behind on an extraordinarily low scoring day was Pete Jordan, who shot 63.

Claar, playing his first competitive round of 1997, began with birdies on the first six holes. It was the best streak to start a round since Andy Dillard birdied the first six at Pebble Beach at the 1992 U.S. Open.

Claar also birdied the ninth hole to make the turn in 29. He then tapped in for birdie on the 10th hole to go eight under. "I was getting excited and started thinking about 59, whichis the kiss of death, of course," said Claar.
He bogeyed the 11th hole from a bunker, and then failed to birdie the short par-five 13th, but finished with birdies on three of the last four holes to finish at 62.
"The course just didn't have the bite it usually has," said Claar. "The greens are soft and holding really well."

Claar also had the advantage, as did almost all of the leaders, of playing in the morning when the winds were less strong. Len Mattiace, at 64, and Scott Simpson and Duffy Waldorf, both 65, were the only players among the afternoon starters to finish in the top 10.
Like Claar, Reid also shot 62 with a bogey. Reid had nine birdies and an eagle through 15 holes on Thursday, but bogeyed the 16th and parred in for his 62.
"Sometimes the hole gets in thh way of the ball," said Reid. "When serendipitous things like this happen you just try to keep your focus. There's plenty of time to look back afterward."

Reid, who has not made it to Sunday in his previous three starts this year and has not played well in recent years but earned a 10-year exemption for winning the 1988 World Series of Golf, said that he had been practicing putting at night on his hotel room carpets.
"I'm glad it's paying off. I putted really well today," he said.
